title: Coin Change
pattern: Unbounded knapsack: fewest coins for every amount
statement: You have coins of the given denominations (as many of each as you like). Return the **fewest** coins needed to make up exactly `amount`, or `-1` if it cannot be done.

example.why: 3 + 3 = 6 uses two coins. (Greedy — always taking the largest coin — would give 4 + 1 + 1, three coins.)

idea: Taking the largest coin first can fail (see the example), so compute the best answer for **every** amount from 0 up to the target.
`dp[a]` = fewest coins that add up to `a`. If the last coin used is `c`, the rest is the amount `a − c`, so `dp[a] = dp[a − c] + 1`.
Try each coin as that last coin and keep the minimum. Amounts that cannot be made stay at ∞.

complexity.timeWhy: Every amount is checked once for every coin.

steps.text: Our example: **`coins = [1,3,4], amount = 6`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
`dp[a]` will hold the fewest coins needed for amount a. ∞ means *not possible (so far)*.
